cohort: 72 pregnant women diagnosed with SARS-CoV-2 infection who delivered at Zoram Medical College Hospital, Mizoram, India
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with various placental pathological changes, including chorangiosis, villositis, and infarction, although these findings did not significantly correlate with neonatal outcomes except for a higher proportion of normal placentas in the asymptomatic group.
mod_finding: The majority of women (93.1%) underwent cesarean delivery, primarily due to SARS-CoV-2 infection (n=49), existing obstetric problems (n=15), or fetal distress (n=5).
